reason: This is a new pattern (proposed catalogue entry T6, 'the fitter's tolerance as a search coordinate'). CMA stream F made the kit's underside quantile q a free coordinate (concept_kit fit_profiles q, clipped to [0.8, 1.0]; fold-sph3r.py evaluate). With q < 1, each rigid underside is fitted below its worst pose's requirement, so the search lowers metal into the 0-2 mm shell in the poses the quantile drops. Measured on the same bench (Bench(60,160) fast, model unchanged), the whole of F's lead comes from q, not from the axes. F's axes at q 1.0 score 50.72 (< 1 mm 50.72, < 2 mm 51.84, lowest metal 1.15 mm, overhead 5 / 12). The same axes at q 0.9805 score 44.72 (53.66 / 76.53, lowest 0.004 mm, overhead 6 / 12). So 6.00 plain points and the extra overhead pose are the quantile. At q 1.0 the design's best is G's 49.03, which beats F's axes at q 1.0 by 1.69. q is not a universal gain: G's axes at q 0.9805 score 52.26 (contact 0.0198, < 2 mm 80.26). Stream F found the axes where the cheap contact cutoff pays. The cutoff is cheap because contact costs 100 x the share of contact poses, while metal at 0.004 mm costs nothing. The design doc says so itself: 'With q < 1, the score buys in-band with contact poses' (docs/concepts/fold-sph3r.md stage 2). Why watch: the shape that comes out is a real rigid shape, and the bench measures it honestly under the plain-gap rule. The gain is metal moved toward the skin, not a better mechanism. Action: any polish or verification of this row runs at q 1.0, with G (49.03) as the shape to carry forward. Across the project, report a q < 1 number beside its q 1.0 twin at the same axes. The same knob holds +41 to +73 fast points in three verified rows at their own axes: arm-parked-knee-4r 19.32 -> 92.19, j3-neck-over-3r 26.26 -> 67.37, zc-frontier-3r 30.04 -> 90.23 at q 1.0 (remeasure/fold-sph3r_proposal_q1_rows.json; a pointer for their next T5 audit, not a finding against them).

reason: The pattern proposed by the raglan-routed-3r audit (catalogue S7, 'out-of-band depth blindness') is present here. Hub 2 is 0.00 in band in every taken clip pose, fitted at F 154 mm from GH (posterolateral, horizontal). Its metal is a median >= 31.75 mm off the skin: 31.75 mm is the fast grid's cap, so that is a floor, not the value. The design doc's exact red team at k2221 puts it at a median 73 mm. Link 2, which spans from hub 2, is 0.10 in band (F) and 0.06 (G). The in-band term cannot tell 15 mm from 70 mm, so the gap would not change if hub 2 sat at 16 mm. The design does not buy points with this (hub 2 cannot come down on any axis set the CMA found, from 6 starts). But the number hides the design's largest profile defect: a hub standing several cm off the back of the shoulder, against the ~1 cm goal.
